svg.title: Compare Sub-Niches on the Same Cost Boundary
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-sub-niche-direct-contribution; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Sub-Niches on the Same Cost Boundary; subtitle: Illustrative contribution before operating overhead, not net margin; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each bar assumes $10,000 of realized resale revenue. Direct costs include acquisition, transport, handling, inspection, and refurbishment; operating overhead, including selling and payment fees, is excluded. These percentages are planning hypotheses, not measured auction yields. An equal-revenue mix averages 24% direct contribution, matching the Base-Case before its 10% overhead allocation.; caption: A larger spread can conceal slower turnover, expensive removal, or unsold inventory. Validate each hypothesis with completed transactions before increasing bid limits.; stages: label: Office furniture bundles; value: 16% direct contribution; numeric value: 16.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $8,400 direct cost leaves $1,600 before overhead. Require confirmed loading access and buyer measurements; bulky low-value pieces can turn storage into the dominant cost.; label: Commercial kitchen equipment; value: 20% direct contribution; numeric value: 20.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $8,000 direct cost leaves $2,000 before overhead. Verify power, gas, refrigeration condition, and installation requirements; unverified functionality can overwhelm repair limits.; label: Fleet vehicles and trailers; value: 24% direct contribution; numeric value: 24.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $7,600 direct cost leaves $2,400 before overhead. Match VINs to sale documents and confirm the state title pathway before allowing transport or repair spending.; label: Grounds-maintenance equipment; value: 28% direct contribution; numeric value: 28.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $7,200 direct cost leaves $2,800 before overhead. Inspect hydraulic systems, hour meters, attachments, and seasonal demand; missing proprietary components can erase the spread.; label: Industrial shop equipment; value: 32% direct contribution; numeric value: 32.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $6,800 direct cost leaves $3,200 before overhead. Confirm rigging access, three-phase power requirements, guarding condition, and a credible buyer before bidding.

text.title: Compare Sub-Niches on the Same Cost Boundary
text.tspan: Compare Sub-Niches on the Same Cost Boundary

circle.title: label: Office furniture bundles; value: 16% direct contribution; numeric value: 16.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $8,400 direct cost leaves $1,600 before overhead. Require confirmed loading access and buyer measurements; bulky low-value pieces can turn storage into the dominant cost.

label: Commercial kitchen equipment; value: 20% direct contribution; numeric value: 20.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $8,000 direct cost leaves $2,000 before overhead. Verify power, gas, refrigeration condition, and installation requirements; unverified functionality can overwhelm repair limits.

label: Fleet vehicles and trailers; value: 24% direct contribution; numeric value: 24.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $7,600 direct cost leaves $2,400 before overhead. Match VINs to sale documents and confirm the state title pathway before allowing transport or repair spending.

label: Grounds-maintenance equipment; value: 28% direct contribution; numeric value: 28.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $7,200 direct cost leaves $2,800 before overhead. Inspect hydraulic systems, hour meters, attachments, and seasonal demand; missing proprietary components can erase the spread.

label: Industrial shop equipment; value: 32% direct contribution; numeric value: 32.0; detail: $10,000 resale less $6,800 direct cost leaves $3,200 before overhead. Confirm rigging access, three-phase power requirements, guarding condition, and a credible buyer before bidding.

text.title: Assumptions: Each bar assumes $10,000 of realized resale revenue. Direct costs include acquisition, transport, handling, inspection, and refurbishment; operating overhead, including selling and payment fees, is excluded. These percentages are planning hypotheses, not measured auction yields. An equal-revenue mix averages 24% direct contribution, matching the Base-Case before its 10% overhead allocation.
